readme.content:
# MCP-KB

Personal dev knowledge base as an MCP server. Log issues and gotchas hit while
working on projects, then let Claude recall them by full-text search before you
re-debug the same thing.

## Storage

SQLite with FTS5 (`porter unicode61` tokenizer, bm25 ranking). The database lives
**outside** this repo so it persists across clones and never gets committed. The
default location is per-platform; override it anywhere with `KB_DB_PATH`:

| OS | Default DB path |
|---|---|
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/mcp-kb/kb.db` or `~/.local/share/mcp-kb/kb.db` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/mcp-kb/kb.db` |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mcp-kb\kb.db` |

## Platforms

Pure Python + stdlib `sqlite3`, no native dependencies — runs on Linux, macOS,
and Windows. FTS5 ships in the official CPython builds (python.org installers,
Homebrew) and most distro packages; the server checks for it at startup and
fails with a clear message if a stripped build lacks it.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `kb_add(project, title, problem, fix?, tags?)` | Save a new entry |
| `kb_search(query, project?, limit?)` | Ranked full-text search |
| `kb_get(entry_id)` | Fetch one full record |
| `kb_recent(limit?, project?)` | Newest-first list |
| `kb_projects()` | Projects with counts |
| `kb_update(entry_id, ...)` | Edit fields (e.g. add `fix` later) |
| `kb_delete(entry_id)` | Remove a record |

## How agents use it

The server ships an `instructions` string (see `INSTRUCTIONS` in
`src/mcp_kb/server.py`) that the MCP client passes to the model, telling it to
use the KB **proactively**:

- **Before** debugging or investigating an error → `kb_search` the symptom
  keywords (with `project` if known) to check for a prior fix.
- **After** resolving a non-obvious bug, config trap, or surprising behavior →
  `kb_add` it (`title`, `problem`, `fix`, `tags`, `project`).
- Log an unsolved problem with an empty `fix`, then `kb_update` it once solved.
- `kb_recent` / `kb_projects` to orient on what is already recorded.

Server `instructions` are advisory — some clients show them, some weight them
lightly. To make the behavior reliable in a given project, also add a line to
that project's `CLAUDE.md`, e.g.:

```
Use the kb_* MCP tools: search the KB before debugging, log gotchas after fixing.
```

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Why | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Python ≥ 3.11 | Runtime (uses `X \| None` typing, modern stdlib) | `python --version` |
| sqlite3 with FTS5 | Search index — bundled in official CPython builds | `python -c "import sqlite3; sqlite3.connect(':memory:').execute('CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(x)')"` (no error = OK) |
| pipx | Isolated, move-proof install | `pipx --version` |
| git | Clone the repo | `git --version` |
| An MCP client | Consumes the server (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) | — |

Install pipx if missing: `python -m pip install --user pipx && pipx ensurepath`
(or `sudo pacman -S python-pipx` on Arch, `brew install pipx` on macOS).

The server itself has one Python dependency, `mcp[cli]`, pulled in automatically
by the install step — no manual install needed.

## Setup (pipx — move-proof)

pipx installs into its own isolated venv, so the binary keeps working even if
this source directory is moved or deleted.

```bash
cd ~/works/MCP-KB
pipx install . --force      # binary -> ~/.local/bin/mcp-kb
```

After editing the code, re-sync the installed copy:

```bash
pipx install ~/works/MCP-KB --force   # or: pipx reinstall mcp-kb
```

## Register with Claude Code (user scope = all projects)

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user kb -- ~/.local/bin/mcp-kb
```

Verify: `claude mcp get kb` (Scope should say "User config"), then `/mcp`
inside a session.

On Windows the pipx binary is `mcp-kb.exe` under `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\`
(run `pipx ensurepath` once so it is on PATH). Any MCP client works — point its
config `command` at the full path to the binary.

## FTS5 query tips

- Plain words are OR-matched: `nginx realip`
- Phrase: `"set_real_ip_from"`
- Boolean: `nginx AND proxy`, `cert NOT letsencrypt`
- Prefix: `prox*`
